observations.text: SP, due to a head-down scan concentrated on the navigation log and the turning point timing, did not check the surrounding space uninterruptedly along the route segment. Converging VFR traffic already reported on the common frequency was not detected and appropriate separation was not established, with the result that the IP called the traffic, directed the avoidance turn and flew part of the segment. Visual lookout technique and the division of the scan between inside and outside the cockpit require further work.

SP, due to attention captured by the navigation display while re-establishing the route, did not maintain the visual check of the surrounding space and did not take the R/T reports into consideration during the leg to the second turning point. Traffic operating in the same VFR corridor went undetected and the aircraft closed inside the separation SP was required to maintain, with the result that the IP took control and executed the avoidance maneuver. Clearing could not be sustained without the IP's assistance.

SP, due to a lookout pattern confined to the sector ahead of the nose, did not clear the airspace into the turn before rolling out over the turning point. Traffic in the unchecked sector was acquired only after the IP's verbal prompt, and separation was opened late instead of at the first opportunity. The error was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the route timing update, did not effectively monitor the R/T and lost the position reports of the other aircraft working the same area. Situational awareness of the surrounding traffic was rebuilt only after the IP prompted a listen-out and a clearing turn, and appropriate separation was re-established late rather than maintained. Recognition and correction of the lapse were delayed.

SP, due to a visual check briefly interrupted while re-setting the chart at the turning point, did not clear the airspace to the left before commencing the turn. SP identified the omission within a few seconds, completed a clearing turn and resumed the uninterrupted outside scan, with the result of a minor error corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to complacency on a route flown repeatedly without conflicting traffic, allowed the check of the surrounding space to become intermittent during the second leg. A traffic report on the common frequency led SP to resume the full lookout and to open the VFR distance from the developing cloud layer, with the result of minor errors identified and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP executed clearing throughout the navigation sortie within the desired standards, checking the surrounding space continuously, detecting nearby moving A/C in time, maintaining appropriate separation and keeping the required VFR distance from clouds. On two occasions, however, the outside scan was resumed only after the navigation task had been finished rather than interleaved with it, and the traffic was acquired later than the R/T report already allowed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more even allocation of attention between the cockpit work and the outside scan is expected to improve.

SP cleared the surrounding space continuously and methodically over every leg, at each turning point and during the recovery into the airport traffic pattern, allocating attention between the navigation task and the outside scan with neither being neglected. All nearby moving A/C were detected before they were called by the IP, appropriate separation and VFR distance from clouds were maintained at all times, and the R/T was monitored effectively so that conflicts were anticipated rather than reacted to. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a scan confined to the instrument panel during the route leg, did not check the surrounding space and did not take the R/T reports into consideration at any point of the navigation profile. Traffic converging from the right was not detected and no avoidance action was initiated, with the result that the IP directed the clearing turn and flew part of the leg. Basic lookout technique and the allocation of attention outside the cockpit require further work.

SP, due to failure to shed the navigation log work when workload increased approaching the turning point, did not resume the visual check of the surrounding space or monitor the R/T for the remainder of the leg. Reported traffic in the same area went undetected and no assessment of separation was made, with the result that the IP identified the conflict and directed the avoidance turn. Clearing was not completed without the IP's assistance.

SP performed clearing within the desired standards for this stage, checking the surrounding space and detecting the nearby traffic, although on two occasions the check was carried out only after the IP's verbal prompt and the flight path correction followed with delay. Appropriate separation and VFR distance from clouds were nevertheless preserved throughout the sortie. Marginal performance for the Training Section - initiation of the outside scan on SP's own judgement, without prompting, is expected to improve.

SP checked the surrounding space on his/her own initiative throughout the route and detected the nearby moving A/C before they were pointed out, maintaining appropriate separation and VFR distance from clouds. The two brief interruptions of the outside scan during the turning point work were identified and corrected by SP in a timely manner, without any verbal prompt or intervention from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP allocated attention accurately between the navigation task and the outside scan, checking the surrounding space uninterruptedly along the route and in the airport traffic pattern. Nearby moving A/C were detected in time, appropriate separation was maintained and the R/T was monitored continuously to build situational awareness, with no verbal prompt or intervention required from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP cleared the surrounding space with exceptional thoroughness, sustaining an uninterrupted lookout through every leg, every turning point and the recovery into the airport traffic pattern with no degradation of the navigation task. Traffic was built from the R/T picture before it became visible, separation was opened early instead of being corrected late, and appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained with a margin throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.
